report_name: CISA Warns of Critical Flaws in IoT, EV Charging, and Access Control Systems

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-101104
vulnerabilities.description: A missing authorization flaw in the Meari IoT Cloud Platform's OpenAPI Service that could allow an authenticated user to manipulate IoT devices they do not own.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-96613
vulnerabilities.description: A missing authorization flaw in the Meari IoT Cloud Platform allowing an attacker to retrieve device shadow information, potentially including credentials and telemetry.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-95102
vulnerabilities.description: A critical unauthenticated WebSocket endpoint vulnerability in the Monta EV-charging platform that could allow an attacker to impersonate a charging station, potentially leading to unauthorized actions.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2023-46604
vulnerabilities.description: A deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability in an embedded Apache ActiveMQ component of the Armatura One access control system, which could lead to arbitrary code execution. This CVE is known to be actively exploited in other products.

identities.name: Meari
identities.description: Vendor of the Meari IoT Cloud Platform, which was found to have multiple missing authorization vulnerabilities for which no patch is available.

identities.name: Monta
identities.description: Vendor of the Monta EV-charging platform, which was found to have a critical unauthenticated WebSocket endpoint vulnerability.

identities.name: Armatura
identities.description: Vendor of the Armatura One access control system, which was found to contain several vulnerabilities, including a known exploited flaw (CVE-2023-46604) in its Apache ActiveMQ component.
